title: A River for the Fallen Leaves

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [gentle river flowing] [softly] Let the body rest and imagine sitting beside a slow river beneath autumn trees.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the experience you are resisting. Name it gently if a name comes: fear... pressure... grief... wanting... no.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel where it lives in the body. Let sensation be a fallen leaf touching water for the first time.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Acceptance is the river making room for the leaf. It does not approve the storm that brought it down.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the urge to push, solve, explain, or cling. Let that urge become another leaf beside the first.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Quietly repeat: this is what is here now... and this moment is allowed to be known.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Observe whether sensation moves, stays, widens, or changes temperature. No movement is required.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] The river is wider than one leaf. Include sounds, breath, contact points, and the room around the difficulty.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If a thought returns, let it touch the surface and travel at its own pace.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] You can accept the reality of this moment and still choose boundaries, repair, or change in the next one.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [faint river flowing] Let the river continue without watching every bend. Feel the body beside it, breathing and supported.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes when ready. Carry the river's spaciousness, not the leaves.
